entry_fields.id: stable slug; prose and pin comments cite this, never the number
entry_fields.claim: one sentence, stated the way the book would state it
entry_fields.value: number, [low, high] range, or structured object
entry_fields.source: title / venue / year / locator (doi or url); for papers, the PINNED version
entry_fields.retrieved: ISO date the value was last checked against the source; year-month permitted for entries ported from book.md's reference section, whose figures were last verified July 2026
entry_fields.method: how the value was obtained: quoted, derived, fetched-by-script
entry_fields.fetch: script under registry/fetch/ that can refresh this value, or null for pinned papers
entry_fields.notes: caveats that must travel with the number
entry_fields.book: which book's claims need this entry: book-1 (Part V/method evidence), book-2 (transition/tech/costing), legacy-only (candidate for the deletion manifest's consciously-dropped list); absent = book-1

claims.claim: During Jharkhand's biometric-authentication reforms, 1.5–2 million legitimate beneficiaries lost access to benefits at some point.
claims.source: Muralidharan, Niehaus & Sukhtankar, "Identity Verification Standards in Welfare Programs: Experimental Evidence from India", Review of Economics and Statistics 107(2): 372-392 (2025), doi:10.1162/rest_a_01296, https://doi.org/10.1162/rest_a_01296

claims.claim: In the reconciliation phase, roughly 1.7 million people did not receive PDS benefits in the first month (July 2017).
claims.source: Muralidharan, Niehaus & Sukhtankar (2025), REStat 107(2), body
claims.notes: ~1.2 million under the paper's conservative assumption. The widely quoted '13%' is a percentage-POINT increase in non-receipt in treated blocks, not a share of all beneficiaries.

claims.claim: 88% of cancelled ration cards sampled in the study districts belonged to genuine households.
claims.source: Muralidharan, Niehaus & Sukhtankar (2025), REStat 107(2)
claims.method: quoted; authors label the figure 'purely descriptive' (non-causal)
claims.notes: Covers the 1.44 lakh cancellations in the 10 study districts — never to be narrated as the Drèze survey's 11 lakh statewide figure.

claims.claim: 11 lakh (1.1 million) ration cards were cancelled in Jharkhand for not being linked to Aadhaar.
claims.source: Drèze, Khalid, Khera & Somanchi, "Aadhaar and Food Security in Jharkhand: Pain without Gain?", Economic and Political Weekly 52(50): 50-60 (16 December 2017), https://www.epw.in/journal/2017/50/special-articles/aadhaar-and-food-security-jharkhand.html

claims.claim: Owen’s New Harmony community began in 1825 and dissolved in 1827; his labour exchanges attempted time-based valuation while still requiring judgments about unlike products and tasks.

The retained claim omits the settler and constitution counts and does not attribute the community’s failure to valuation alone.

claims.claim: Lin proposes that removal of collective members’ right to withdraw in 1958 undermined a self-enforcing agreement and contributed to the agricultural productivity collapse; the paper presents evidence consistent with that hypothesis.
claims.source: Lin, "Collectivization and China's Agricultural Crisis in 1959-1961", Journal of Political Economy 98(6): 1228-1252 (1990), doi:10.1086/261732, https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/abs/10.1086/261732; Lin, AER 82(1): 34-51 (1992); Li, Journal of Agrarian Change 18(1): 67-86 (2018)
claims.notes: Nine cases. The 1958 removal of the exit right re-checked 2026-09-19 against the published abstract and summaries of the JPE article. Lin's exit-rights thesis is contested: the 1993 Journal of Comparative Economics symposium collects the criticisms, and Li (2018) is the egalitarianism reading. Part V argues the exit right, which is the part the design turns on, not the famine's full causation. Interpretation clarified 2026-09-19: Part V attributes the causal explanation to Lin and does not present it as an isolated effect or a settled account of the entire crisis.

claims.claim: Abramitzky examines equal sharing, selection, exit and incentive pressures in the kibbutzim. Roughly three-quarters had adopted differential salaries by around 2011; the account does not isolate leadership rotation as the cause of reform.
claims.source: Abramitzky, "Lessons from the Kibbutz on the Equality-Incentives Trade-Off", Journal of Economic Perspectives 25(1): 185-208 (2011), doi:10.1257/jep.25.1.185, https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/jep.25.1.185; Abramitzky, The Mystery of the Kibbutz, Princeton UP (2018)
claims.notes: Nine cases. The 1999–2011 differential-salary series was checked against published descriptions of the reform literature; the JEP article is the source of record. Part V’s approximate three-in-four share concerns around 2011. Its approximately 270 communities also belong to the study period (the 2011 abstract reports 268), not a current census. Neither figure isolates leadership rotation as the cause, and the chapter does not infer that a universal minimum requires equal pay.

claims.claim: Nyerere's villagization: voluntary from the 1967 Arusha Declaration, compulsory from 1973, with at least five million people relocated on Scott's own estimate; totals for how many ended up in villages are contested and run far higher.
claims.source: Scott, Seeing Like a State, Yale UP (1998), ch. 7, https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctt1nq3vk
claims.notes: Scott’s relocation estimate and the higher totals for village residents measure different populations. The latter totals are disputed. Part V does not combine them into a count of coerced moves, infer a cause from their disagreement, or claim Scott proved a named total was padded. The case concerns coercive relocation justified as collective improvement; it does not establish that every public service is coercive.

claims.claim: Chile's Cybersyn: real-time economic coordination cut short; what the technology could and could not have carried.
claims.source: Medina, Cybernetic Revolutionaries: Technology and Politics in Allende's Chile, MIT Press (2011), ISBN 9780262525961, https://mitpress.mit.edu/9780262525961/cybernetic-revolutionaries/
claims.notes: Nine cases. The monograph is the source of record. Part V omits the disputed telex-machine count. The coup’s termination of the project does not establish how it would have performed over time or prove technical success or failure.

claims.claim: In the bundled 141-country snapshot, the correlation between electoral democracy and mean life evaluation is about 0.51 before, and about 0.20 after, adjusting for log GDP per capita. This is descriptive association, not a causal allocation between income and democracy.
claims.source: Derived by registry/fetch/vdem_happiness.py from OWID grapher series (CC BY): electoral-democracy-index (V-Dem v2x_polyarchy) https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/electoral-democracy-index, happiness-cantril-ladder (WHR) https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/happiness-cantril-ladder, gdp-per-capita-worldbank https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-worldbank; latest observation per series, each year ≥ 2022 (years can differ within a country); snapshot registry/data/vdem-happiness-2026-08-03.csv
claims.notes: Snapshot reproduced 2026-09-19. Countries are equally weighted; three GDP observations are from 2024 while the other year labels are 2025. Adjustment can remove confounding or part of a causal pathway; this analysis does not identify which. It establishes neither material provision as the cause of most wellbeing differences nor an ordering of political and material rights. See book-1/source/vdem-rederivation.md.

claims.claim: In the bundled cross-section, adjacent Regimes of the World category means differ by +0.02, +0.59 and +1.09 Cantril-ladder points. These compare different groups of countries and do not estimate gains from regime transitions.
claims.source: Same derivation as vdem-2026-democracy-happiness-partial, adding the OWID political-regime series for the Regimes of the World categories https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/political-regime
claims.notes: Snapshot reproduced 2026-09-19. Category means are unadjusted for income and other country differences. Steps use unrounded means. The small lowest-category difference is not evidence that partial democratisation has no benefit. A cross-section does not supply a transition counterfactual.

claims.claim: The exploratory absolute-residual regression on the bundled V-Dem snapshot has a negative democracy coefficient after income adjustment. Its uncertainty is sensitive to measurement choices; it does not measure a guaranteed wellbeing floor or the lower tail of individual lives.
claims.source: Same derivation as vdem-2026-democracy-happiness-partial (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/electoral-democracy-index and siblings); the isolation test against the alternative index is recorded qualitatively in book-1/source/vdem-rederivation.md, its coefficients deliberately kept out of this CC0 registry under the 2026-08-02 licensing ruling
claims.notes: Snapshot reproduced 2026-09-19. Absolute residuals include both tails of a fitted line through country means; standard errors are conventional, not heteroskedasticity-robust. The archived same-sample EIU comparison also has a negative coefficient but does not pass the conventional significance threshold. That contrast does not test a difference between coefficients, prove the phenomenon false, or identify a causal effect. No EIU-derived values are reproduced in this CC0 registry. Working-record interpretations are superseded by its 2026-09-19 correction.

claims.claim: The prior democracy/happiness analysis behind Part V's worked example, independently re-derived on openly licensed instruments (source reference only).
claims.source: demo-happy.txt (repository root), computed over democracy_vs_happiness_144.csv: WHR 2025 life evaluations (2022–2024 average) merged with EIU Democracy Index 2025, 144 countries matched from EIU's 166 and WHR's 147
claims.notes: PRIOR ANALYSIS, RECORDED FOR PROVENANCE, NOT AS EVIDENCE. Every figure Part V uses comes from the V-Dem re-derivation (vdem-2026-*), and no EIU-derived value enters this CC0 registry, per the 2026-08-02 licensing ruling. The re-derivation reproduced the income narrowing and the step pattern and did NOT reproduce this analysis's headline dispersion finding — see vdem-2026-floor-claim-instrument-fragile. The merged CSV sits in the repository root under the root LICENSE, committed before that ruling, and carries EIU index values; whether the repository may grant CC0 over a non-redistributable index is an open question for the author, recorded in CLAUDE.md under the pending obligations that outlived the retired root tracker.

claims.claim: Santoshi Kumari, eleven, died on 28 September 2017 in Simdega district, Jharkhand, months after her family's ration card was cancelled for want of an Aadhaar link; her family said she died asking for rice, and the district administration said the cause was malaria rather than starvation.
claims.source: Scroll.in, "Jharkhand death: Girl dies of hunger because her family did not have an Aadhaar-linked ration card" (October 2017), https://scroll.in/article/854225/denied-food-because-she-did-not-have-aadhaar-linked-ration-card-jharkhand-girl-dies-of-starvation; Scroll.in, "Remembering Santoshi Kumari: a year after" (2018), https://scroll.in/article/895667/a-year-after-jharkhand-girl-died-of-starvation-aadhaar-tragedies-are-on-the-rise
claims.notes: The cancellation is not in dispute: the block development officer confirmed the family's card was deleted for want of an Aadhaar link, and the family was eligible under the National Food Security Act. The CAUSE OF DEATH IS DISPUTED — activists and the family said starvation, the district administration said malaria — and any use of this entry must carry that dispute. Part V argues the cancellation and the family's account, attributed, and does not assert the cause.

claims.claim: EPI estimates that realized CEO compensation at the largest 350 US firms was about 325 times typical-worker compensation in 2025.
claims.units: ratio of CEO compensation to average compensation of production and nonsupervisory workers in the firms’ industries
claims.source: Bivens, Gould and Kandra, CEO Pay, Economic Policy Institute (15 September 2026), Figure A and its methods notes, https://www.epi.org/publication/ceo-pay/
claims.notes: Rechecked against the 2026 table and definition. Typical worker means an industry average for production and nonsupervisory workers, not a median employee at each firm or its lowest-paid worker. The 2025 figure is an estimate. Part V gives its rough scale and does not calculate a governance effect from unlike MONDRAGON and EPI ratios. Earlier mixed-vintage values and the median gloss are superseded.

claims.claim: Adjustment for a regression covariate can alter the causal quantity of interest; whether a control helps depends on the causal structure.
claims.source: Cinelli, Carlos, Andrew Forney and Judea Pearl. A Crash Course in Good and Bad Controls. Sociological Methods & Research 53(3), 1071–1104 (2024; online 2022). https://doi.org/10.1177/00491241221099552; author-hosted reprint https://ftp.cs.ucla.edu/pub/stat_ser/r493-reprint.pdf
claims.notes: Methodological reference for Part V; no empirical estimate about this constitution or causal estimate of democracy is attributed to this source.

claims.claim: A contrast between a statistically significant estimate and a nonsignificant estimate does not itself establish a statistically significant difference between them.
claims.source: Gelman, Andrew and Hal Stern. The Difference Between Significant and Not Significant Is Not Itself Statistically Significant. The American Statistician 60(4), 328–331 (2006). https://doi.org/10.1198/000313006X152649; author-hosted copy https://sites.stat.columbia.edu/gelman/surveys.course/GelmanStern2006.pdf
claims.notes: Methodological reference for Part V; no empirical estimate about this constitution or causal estimate of democracy is attributed to this source.

claims.claim: Scientific conclusions should not turn only on whether a p-value crosses a threshold; statistical significance does not measure effect size or practical importance.
claims.source: American Statistical Association, Statement on Statistical Significance and P-Values (2016). https://www.amstat.org/asa/files/pdfs/p-valuestatement.pdf; full statement https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.2016.1154108
claims.notes: Methodological reference for Part V; no empirical estimate about this constitution or causal estimate of democracy is attributed to this source.
